name: B10-0492/2025 – Motion for a resolution
title: MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the draft Commission implementing decision renewing the authorisation for the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified cotton MON 88913 (MON-88913-8), pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 1829/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council
part_text:
The European Parliament is asking the European Commission to withdraw its plan to renew the licence for a genetically modified cotton, MON 88913. The cotton is engineered to tolerate glyphosate, a weedkiller the Parliament links to health and environmental concerns. Parliament says the safety review was too narrow: it looked at no new long-term feeding studies and did not examine combined or indirect effects. Parliament also wants the Commission to propose new rules for deciding on genetically modified organisms, because Member States often fail to reach a majority.

- Nothing changes yet: Parliament only asks the Commission to withdraw its plan and not renew the licence.
- It affects the Commission, Member States, and companies that sell or use this cotton and its products.
- Next, the Commission decides whether to withdraw, and Parliament wants new rules on genetically modified organism approvals.
